transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-27
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortega (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Pegasus Head of Data), Sofia Martinez (Pegasus ML Eng), Jordan Lee (CTO)

Summary (auto): quick econ playback, we ran dedicated and hosted configs; caching results looked promising; customer concerned about p95 latency for interactive product; next steps agreed.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): ok hi everyone thanks for hopping on, appreciate the time. quick agenda — 1) short playback of the numbers from last 48h pilot run, 2) dig into tokens per dollar and where savings came from, 3) batching/caching tradeoffs and latency, 4) next steps. anything to add?
[00:32] Ravi (Pegasus): no that's great. we mostly want to see whether the numbers actually move the needle for our cost model. remember we have a bunch of short prompts (2-6 tokens per request) and some long form summarization.
[00:50] Liam (Redwood SE): yeah great, i'll start with the run summary. so we did two main runs: hosted burst on a multi-tenant A100 pool and a dedicated H100 reserve. workloads were replayed with your supplied mix — about 78% interactive short-turns, 22% long summarization.
[01:10] Liam: raw throughput on the H100 with base model (fp16) was ~950 tokens/sec observed under sustained load; after enabling continuous prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts we saw effective tokens/sec/$ improve to roughly 1.3k tokens/sec and cost per 1M tokens dropped from $X to $Y — net of about 28-35% improvement depending on cache hit rate. (note: this is approximate, see sheet).
[01:45] Sofia (Pegasus): quick q — when you say cache hit rate, what's the distribution across short prompts vs long? our short prompts are highly repetitive but slightly templated.
[01:55] Liam: good question. hit rate for short interactive prompts was ~62% for exact-prefix matches; for long summaries it was under 8% because prompts are more unique. overall effective hit ~48%. you could expect higher if you canonicalize prompts.
[02:20] Ravi: ok that aligns with what we suspected. any latency impact for cache hits? our product needs sub-200ms p95 for the interactive flow.
[02:31] Liam: cache hits were sub-25ms added overhead on top of model tokenization; end-to-end p95 for interactive prompts on dedicated H100 with small batching (batch size 4, inter-request timeout 15ms) stayed at ~180-220ms depending on prompt length. so we're close to your 200ms SLO; some tails over.
[02:58] Jordan (CTO): when you say tails, what's the 99th? we can't have long tails for customer-facing interactive features.
[03:10] Liam: 99th was around 420ms in the worst slot during a burst. that was correlating with larger batching events and an occasional context-swap on the GPU. we can tune batching window and enable stricter latency SLO routing to low-latency nodes to bring p99 down. tradeoff is cost because smaller batching decreases tokens/sec/$ efficiency.
[03:37] Maya: right this is the classic latency vs cost tradeoff — we can prioritize latency for the interactive route and route summarization to a cheaper lane or quantized variant.
[03:50] Sofia: is quantization safe for our summarization task? we care about factuality and no hallucinations.
[03:58] Liam: we tested 4-bit quantized variant on the dedicated run for a subset of summarization prompts. quality was within margin on ROUGE and answer fidelity checks for ~92% of cases, but there were edge failures on long-chain reasoning prompts. We'll produce a short quality-check report.
[04:20] Ravi: okay, that's fine — summarization can tolerate slightly lower fidelity but not hallucination. can you quantify the cost delta with quant?
[04:28] Liam: quantized path reduced cost per 1M tokens by roughly 22% compared to fp16 on the H100 test. combined with caching for repetitive tokens in long outputs, total savings could be up to ~40% for that route. again depends on prompt characteristics.
[04:50] Maya: i just uploaded an updated pricing workbook to the shared drive; link is in the chat — it includes scenarios: hosted multi-tenant, dedicated reserved monthly, and hybrid with routing rules.
[05:03] Jordan: saw that, thanks. question on burst protection — if we reserve, can we still handle spikes? we don't want request throttling.
[05:13] Liam: yes you can configure burstable capacity with autoscale buffers; reserved gives baseline throughput and we allow burst to a higher pool at a premium. there's a graceful fallback policy to cheaper models if both pools are saturated.
[05:28] Sofia: what about prefix canonicalization — you mentioned that could raise cache hit rate. that's something we can do in-app — how much effort?
[05:35] Liam: low-medium effort; you'd normalize variable data, hash canonical prompts server-side before sending. we can show a quick example in the integration doc. often yields 10-30% absolute hit rate improvement depending on prompt templates.
[05:52] Ravi: cool. can you run an experiment where we canonicalize and re-run the 24h test? that's probably the most realistic number for us.
[06:00] Liam: yep we can do that. propose: 24h sustained on H100 with canonicalized prompts and the same arrival pattern. we'll log p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec/$ across windows.
[06:12] Maya: action item there for liam. also I'll push the updated pricing scenarios and highlight the tokens/sec/$ assumption column.
[06:20] Jordan: procurement question — what's needed to get to PO? SOC2, contract and a pilot appendix?
[06:28] Maya: yes SOC2 and ISO package are standard; I'll attach the security pack and a pilot PO template. For enterprise we also offer private deployment options (VPC) if you need network isolation.
[06:40] Jordan: we do want VPC for production eventually but pilot can be hosted. what's the data retention policy during pilot?
[06:47] Liam: by default logs are retained for 30 days; we can enable no-retention for token data for the pilot and set up encrypted key management integrations. details in the security pack.
[06:58] Sofia: one more technical — your batching window is adaptive? we saw some bursts causing larger batches which increased p99.
[07:06] Liam: yes adaptive, but you can set soft and hard limits and an inter-request timeout. for interactive routes we recommend small hard limits (batch size <=6, timeout 10-15ms). for background summarization increase batch size for cost savings.
[07:24] Ravi: so what's the expected tokens/sec/$ if we optimize for latency and canonicalize?
[07:30] Liam: rough estimate: interactive lane (low latency) about 700 tokens/sec effective at cost C1; with canonicalization maybe 900 tokens/sec; summarization lane (quant + batching + cache) could reach 1.6-1.9k tokens/sec effective. blended depends on traffic mix.
[07:50] Maya: i've added a sample scenario in the workbook showing blended cost for your 78/22 split. gives about 32% savings vs baseline multi-tenant no-cache setup.
[08:02] Jordan: what's the plan to monitor quality regressions during quant deployment? we can't push blindly.
[08:10] Liam: we run automatic evals on a curated prompt set and a daily sample of production responses with threshold alerts. if deviation exceeds X% we rollback to higher-fidelity variant automatically. we can include that in the pilot checklist.
[08:25] Sofia: perfect. also we want an endpoint with stricter RBAC for our prod keys.
[08:32] Maya: that's supported — per-route API keys, token scoping and SSO integrations. i'll include an RBAC doc.
[08:40] (brief cross talk)
[08:45] Liam: ok to recap next steps — liam runs canonicalized 24h run on H100 and uploads metrics; maya sends pricing workbook + security pack + pilot PO; sofia provides final prompt set; jordan confirms procurement stakeholders. aim to reconvene next week to review results.
[09:10] Ravi: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[09:15] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.

End of transcript.
note: References: shared pricing workbook (link in chat), security pack (SOC2/ISO), benchmark sheet 'pegasus-h100-2026-12' in shared drive
